lines.text: The carton hasn't even tipped, and your tray is already out of the way.
"How did you know?" You were about to say that.
Your brain lives in the past.
Everything you see is at least eighty milliseconds old.
You see ten whole seconds ahead.
So, what if you could see ten seconds into the future?
On top of the real world, you see a pale ghost of it, ten seconds ahead.
Only what your own eyes would see.
And only the future where you do nothing.
Move, and the ghost moves with you.
You know who gets picked, and you know the answer.

The claw machine at the arcade.
You just wait for the ghost to grab.

You hear "Surprise!" ten seconds before anyone yells it.

You live ten seconds away from all of them.
And you see every accident before it happens.
A ball rolling into the street.
A cyclist about to hit a car door.
Futures changed: one hundred and twelve.
When you stop a disaster, nobody ever sees the disaster.

One Friday, you ride with him.

One week later, that yellow gets its extra second.
Voss shakes his hand without looking at him.
